sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *No es que* + subjunctive, *sino que* + indicative from B2 Unit 5. It rejects a reason someone might assume and gives the real one. It is useful here, because people often assume that a country without an army has no security: *No es que Costa Rica no tenga seguridad, sino que la dan policías civiles*.

sections.title: The pattern
rows: the reason you reject: No es que Costa Rica no tenga policía, …
the true reason: … sino que no tiene ejército.
in the past: No era que el país no necesitara seguridad, …
… sino que la daba la policía.

sections.title: About a country without an army

items.spanish: No es que Costa Rica no tenga policía, sino que no tiene ejército.
items.english: It is not that Costa Rica has no police, but that it has no army.

items.spanish: No es que Costa Rica no necesite seguridad, sino que la da una policía civil.
items.english: It is not that Costa Rica does not need security, but that civilian police provide it.

items.spanish: No es que la guerra civil de 1948 fuera larga, sino que fue muy violenta.
items.english: It is not that the 1948 civil war was long, but that it was very violent.

items.spanish: No es que Figueres quisiera el poder para siempre, sino que prometió una nueva Constitución.
items.english: It is not that Figueres wanted power forever, but that he promised a new Constitution.

sections.content: Do not use the indicative after *no es que*: not *No es que no tiene*. And do not drop *que* after *sino*: not *sino no tiene*.
